chapters.title: A Living Hope
chapters.html:
1 Peter 1

Greeting

1Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen exiles of the Dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia,

2chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, by the Spirit who makes you holy, for obedience and for sprinkling with the blood of Jesus Christ: grace and peace be multiplied to you.

Born Again to a Living Hope

3Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who in His great mercy has caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,

4to an inheritance that cannot perish, be defiled or fade away, kept in heaven for you,

5who by the power of God are being guarded through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.

6In this you rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, you have been grieved by various trials,

7so that the testing of your faith, more precious than gold, which perishes though it is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.

8Though you have not seen Him, you love Him. Though you do not see Him now, you believe in Him and rejoice with joy that is inexpressible and filled with glory,

9obtaining the outcome of your faith, the salvation of your souls.

10Concerning this salvation, the prophets who prophesied about the grace that was to be yours searched and inquired carefully,

11inquiring what time, or what kind of time, the Spirit of Christ in them was pointing to when He foretold the sufferings of Christ and the glories that would follow.

12It was revealed to them that they were serving not themselves but you, in the things that have now been announced to you through those who preached the good news to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, things into which angels long to look.

Be Holy

13So prepare your minds for action, be fully sober, and set your hope on the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.

14As obedient children, do not be shaped by the desires you had before, in your ignorance,

15but as He who called you is holy, you also be holy in all your conduct,

16since it is written, "You shall be holy, because I am holy."

17If you call on Him as Father who judges impartially according to each one's work, conduct yourselves with fear throughout the time you live here as guests,

18knowing that you were ransomed from the empty way of life handed down from your fathers, not with perishable things such as silver or gold,

19but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without defect or spot.

20He was foreknown before the foundation of the world, but was revealed in the last times for your sake,

21who through Him believe in God, who raised Him from the dead and gave Him glory, so that your faith and hope are in God.

22Having purified your souls by your obedience to the truth, for a sincere brotherly love, love one another earnestly from the heart,

23since you have been born again, not of perishable seed but of imperishable, through the living and abiding word of God.

24For
"All flesh is like grass,
and all its glory like the flower of grass.
The grass withers,
and the flower falls,

25but the word of the Lord remains forever."
This word is the good news that was preached to you.

Notes

  • vv13–19 "prepare your minds for action… the time you live here as guests… a lamb without defect" — v13 reads literally girding up the loins of your mind, the dress of the first Passover, your waists belted… You shall eat it in haste (Exodus 12:11). The lamb of that night was a lamb without defect (Exodus 12:5); the word of v19, amōmos, is the Greek law's word for an offering without defect (amōmon, Leviticus 22:21), where the Greek of Exodus 12:5 has teleion, perfect. Peter writes to exiles (v1) who live as guests (v17) and were ransomed with a lamb's blood, as Israel was on the way out of Egypt.

  • vv24–25 "All flesh is like grass… but the word of the Lord remains forever" — Isaiah 40:6–8 in the Greek. The Hebrew reads all its loyalty, chasdo, where the Greek has all the glory of man, and the word of our God will stand forever, where Peter has the word of the Lord.

chapters.title: A Living Stone and a Chosen People
chapters.html:
1 Peter 2

The Living Stone

1So put away all malice and all deceit, hypocrisy and envy, and all slander.

2Like newborn babies, long for the pure milk of the word, so that by it you may grow up to salvation,

3if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is good.

4Come to Him, a living stone, rejected by men but chosen and precious in God's sight,

5and you yourselves, like living stones, are being built up as a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.

6For it stands in Scripture:
"I am laying in Zion a stone,
a chosen and precious cornerstone,
and whoever believes in Him will not be put to shame."

7So the honor is for you who believe; but for those who do not believe,
"The stone the builders rejected
has become the cornerstone,"

8and
"a stone to strike against and a rock to stumble over."
They stumble because they disobey the word; to this they were also appointed.

A Chosen People

9But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for His own possession, so that you may proclaim the excellencies of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.

10Once you were not a people, but now you are the people of God; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.

Living as Guests

11Beloved, I urge you as guests and exiles to keep away from the desires of the flesh, which wage war against the soul.

12Keep your conduct among the Gentiles good, so that when they speak against you as evildoers, they may see your good works and glorify God on the day of visitation.

13Submit yourselves for the Lord's sake to every human institution, whether to the king as supreme,

14or to governors as sent by him to punish those who do evil and to praise those who do good.

15For this is the will of God, that by doing good you should silence the ignorance of foolish people.

16Live as free people, not using your freedom as a cover for evil, but as servants of God.

17Honor everyone. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honor the king.

The Example of Christ's Suffering

18Household servants, be subject to your masters with all fear, not only to the good and gentle but also to the crooked.

19For this is grace, when someone, because he is mindful of God, endures sorrows while suffering unjustly.

20For what credit is it if, when you sin and are beaten for it, you endure? But if you do good and suffer for it and endure, this is grace before God.

21For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you might follow in His steps.

22He committed no sin,
and no deceit was found in His mouth.

23When He was insulted, He did not insult in return; when He suffered, He did not threaten, but entrusted Himself to Him who judges justly.

24He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree, so that we might die to sins and live to righteousness. By His wounds you have been healed.

25For you were straying like sheep, but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.

Notes

  • v2 "the pure milk of the word" — to logikon adolon gala. Logikos is built on logos, word, the living and abiding word of God that has just been named (1:23–25), and it also means of the mind, spiritual, as in Paul's reasonable worship (Romans 12:1). Adolon, pure, is literally without deceit, against all deceit, dolos, put away in v1.

  • vv6–8 "a stone… the cornerstone… a stone to strike against" — three stones from three books: Isaiah 28:16 in the Greek, Psalm 118:22, and Isaiah 8:14. Isaiah's Hebrew ends whoever believes will not be in haste; the Greek, which Peter quotes, will not be put to shame. The stone that is a foundation for those who believe is the one others stumble over.

  • vv9–10 "a royal priesthood, a holy nation… once you were not a people" — the words of Sinai in the Greek, you will be for Me a royal priesthood and a holy nation (Exodus 19:6; the Hebrew has a kingdom of priests), and of Isaiah 43:20–21, My chosen people… that they might declare My praise. Not a people… not received mercy are Hosea's children, Lo-ammi and Lo-ruhamah, renamed My people (Hosea 1:9; 2:23).

  • vv22–25 "no deceit was found in His mouth… He Himself bore our sins… by His wounds… like sheep" — Isaiah 53 in the Greek, in order: no deceit in his mouth (v9); he bears our sins (v4); by his wound we were healed, tō mōlōpi, the word of v24 (v5); All we like sheep have gone astray (v6).

chapters.title: A Defense of the Hope
chapters.html:
1 Peter 3

Wives and Husbands

1In the same way, wives, be subject to your own husbands, so that even if some do not obey the word, they may be won without a word by the conduct of their wives,

2when they see your pure conduct, lived in fear.

3Do not let your adorning be outward: braiding the hair, putting on gold jewelry, or wearing fine clothes;

4but let it be the hidden person of the heart, with the imperishable beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious in God's sight.

5For this is how the holy women who hoped in God also adorned themselves long ago, being subject to their own husbands,

6as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord. You have become her children if you do good and do not fear anything that terrifies.

7Husbands, in the same way, live with your wives with understanding, giving honor to the woman as the weaker vessel, since they are heirs with you of the grace of life, so that your prayers may not be hindered.

Suffering for Doing Good

8Finally, all of you, be of one mind, sympathetic, loving as brothers, tenderhearted, humble in mind,

9not repaying evil for evil or insult for insult, but on the contrary blessing, for to this you were called, so that you may inherit a blessing.

10For
"Whoever would love life
and see good days,
let him keep his tongue from evil
and his lips from speaking deceit;

11let him turn away from evil and do good;
let him seek peace and pursue it.

12For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous,
and His ears are open to their prayer,
but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil."

13Who is there to harm you if you are eager for what is good?

14But even if you should suffer for righteousness' sake, you are blessed. Do not fear their fear, and do not be troubled,

15but in your hearts regard the Lord Christ as holy, always ready to make a defense to anyone who asks you for a reason for the hope that is in you;

16yet do it with gentleness and fear, keeping a good conscience, so that when you are slandered, those who abuse your good conduct in Christ may be put to shame.

17For it is better to suffer for doing good, if that should be God's will, than for doing evil.

Christ Suffered Once for Sins

18For Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, so that He might bring you to God, put to death in the flesh but made alive in the spirit,

19in which He also went and preached to the spirits in prison,

20who once disobeyed, when God's patience waited in the days of Noah while the ark was being built, in which a few, that is, eight souls, were brought safely through water.

21Baptism, which corresponds to this, now saves you also — not the removal of dirt from the flesh, but the appeal of a good conscience toward God — through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,

22who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, with angels and authorities and powers made subject to Him.

Notes

  • v6 "as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord" — Genesis 18:12, where Sarah laughs to herself, and my husband is old. The Hebrew word is adoni, my lord, and the Greek ho kyrios mou. Peter takes the title from Sarah's words to herself as she laughs at the promise.

  • vv14–15 "Do not fear their fear… regard the Lord Christ as holy" — Isaiah 8:12–13 in the Greek, Do not fear its fear, and do not be troubled. The Lord Himself, regard Him as holy. In the Hebrew it is The LORD of hosts — Him you shall regard as holy. Peter writes the Lord Christ in the place of the Lord of Isaiah. Their fear can be the fear they feel, or the fear they try to put into you.

  • vv18–20 "made alive in the spirit, in which He also went and preached to the spirits in prison" — pneumati, set against sarki, in the flesh: the spirit of Christ as against His body, or the Holy Spirit by whom He was raised. En hō, in which, can also mean at which time. Peter names the spirits only as those who once disobeyed… in the days of Noah, and says no more of who they are or what was preached.

  • v21 "the appeal of a good conscience toward God" — eperōtēma, found only here in the New Testament, from the verb to ask: a request, an appeal. It can be the appeal to God for a good conscience, or what a good conscience asks of God, or answers Him.

chapters.title: Stewards of God's Grace
chapters.html:
1 Peter 4

Living for the Will of God

1Since Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves also with the same way of thinking, for whoever has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin,

2so as to live the rest of the time in the flesh no longer for human desires but for the will of God.

3The time that is past is enough for doing what the Gentiles want to do, living in sensuality, lusts, drunkenness, revels, drinking parties and lawless idolatry.

4They are surprised that you do not run with them into the same flood of debauchery, and they speak abusively;

5but they will give account to Him who is ready to judge the living and the dead.

6For this is why the good news was preached even to the dead, so that, though judged in the flesh as people are, they might live in the spirit as God does.

Stewards of God's Grace

7The end of all things is near. So be clear-minded and sober for prayer.

8Above all, keep your love for one another earnest, since love covers a multitude of sins.

9Show hospitality to one another without grumbling.

10As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good stewards of God's varied grace:

11whoever speaks, as one speaking the words of God; whoever serves, as by the strength that God supplies, so that in everything God may be glorified through Jesus Christ. To Him belong the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.

Suffering as a Christian

12Beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery trial that has come upon you to test you, as though something strange were happening to you.

13But rejoice insofar as you share in the sufferings of Christ, so that you may also rejoice and be glad when His glory is revealed.

14If you are insulted for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon you.

15But let none of you suffer as a murderer or a thief or an evildoer, or as a meddler.

16Yet if anyone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God in that name.

17For it is time for judgment to begin with the household of God; and if it begins with us, what will be the end of those who do not obey the gospel of God?

18If the righteous is scarcely saved, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?

19So let those who suffer according to God's will entrust their souls to a faithful Creator while doing good.

Notes

  • v6 "the good news was preached even to the dead" — nekrois, with no article: those who are dead now, to whom the gospel came while they lived, or the dead themselves. The verse before has just named the living and the dead as those who will be judged.

  • v11 "To Him belong the glory and the dominion" — hō, to whom, follows God and Jesus Christ in the one clause, and may point to either.

  • v14 "the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon you" — the verb of Isaiah 11:2 in the Greek, the Spirit of God will rest on him, anapausetai, said of a shoot from the stump of Jesse (11:1). What Isaiah says of the shoot of Jesse, Peter says of those insulted for the name of Christ.

  • v18 "If the righteous is scarcely saved" — Proverbs 11:31 in the Greek. The Hebrew reads If the righteous is repaid on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner!

chapters.title: The Chief Shepherd
chapters.html:
1 Peter 5

Shepherd the Flock

1So I urge the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and one who shares in the glory that is going to be revealed:

2shepherd the flock of God that is among you, watching over it, not under compulsion but willingly, as God would have it; not for shameful gain but eagerly;

3not lording it over those in your charge, but being examples to the flock.

4When the Chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.

5In the same way, you who are younger, be subject to the elders. All of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, for "God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble."

Cast Your Anxiety on Him

6Humble yourselves, then, under the mighty hand of God, so that at the proper time He may exalt you,

7casting all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.

8Be sober; be watchful. Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.

9Resist him, firm in your faith, knowing that the same kinds of suffering are being laid on your brotherhood throughout the world.

10After you have suffered a little while, the God of all grace, who called you to His eternal glory in Christ, will Himself restore, establish, strengthen and settle you.

11To Him be the dominion forever and ever. Amen.

Final Greetings

12Through Silvanus, a faithful brother as I regard him, I have written to you briefly, encouraging you and testifying that this is the true grace of God. Stand firm in it.

13She who is in Babylon, chosen together with you, greets you, and so does Mark, my son.

14Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace to all of you who are in Christ.

Notes

  • v13 "She who is in Babylon, chosen together with you" — hē en Babylōni syneklektē, a woman's word with no noun: a church, chosen as the readers are (1:1), or a woman known to them. Babylon may be the city on the Euphrates, or a name, as Revelation names Babylon the great… the great city that rules over the kings of the earth (Revelation 17:5, 18).
